Closes #19003

The operator matrix is unpinned, not untested. The indirect specs elsewhere in this tier assert *that* filtering happened; nothing asserted *what an operator decided*, so one could start returning `true` for a case it used to reject and no test would notice.

`test/playwright/unit/collection/FilterOperators.spec.mjs`, 197 lines, `setup()` first and copied in shape from `Base.spec.mjs`.

## What is asserted

- **One assertion iterates `static operators`** rather than hand-listing it, so an operator added to the array without a matching static function fails there and names itself. The array's contents and order are also pinned, since the class doc comment no longer describes them accurately.
- **A true case and a false case for every operator**, at a boundary value rather than the middle of a range, with values written out literally.
- **The four places the surface surprises**, each read off a live `Filter` before it was written down rather than inferred from the names:
  - `included` / `excluded` take the **collection as the second argument**, because `isFiltered` passes the record first and the filter value second. The empty collection is asserted: nothing is included, everything is excluded.
  - `isFiltered` returns `!Filter[operator](...)`, so `true` means filtered **out**. Asserted in both directions, plus the null-item path.
  - `like` folds case, coerces a non-string record, and matches on an empty needle since every string contains the empty string.
  - `isDefined` / `isUndefined` separate `null` from `undefined`: `null` is defined, only `undefined` is not.
- **`doesNotStartWith` pinned as it behaves**, including that it is the exact inverse of `startsWith` case-folded, and that an empty prefix means every string starts with it. It has no doc comment, so behaviour is the only source available.
- **The both-`Date` coercion**, with the boundary case that documents what does *not* take it: two `Date` objects for one instant are equal under `===`, a `Date` against a number is not, and both-numbers is equal again.

Deterministic throughout: fixed ISO strings, no `new Date()` without an argument, no locale, no dependence on test order.

## How I ran it

```bash
npm install
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/collection/
# → 41 passed, including 8 from this file
```

Not a bare `npx playwright test`.

## Mutations the spec catches

Each mutation was applied to `src/collection/Filter.mjs` locally, run, and reverted. The file is unchanged in the commit.

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| case fold dropped from `doesNotStartWith` | 1 failed |
| negation removed from `isFiltered` | 1 failed |
| `isDefined` conflating `null` with `undefined` | 1 failed |

Without these the suite would describe today's behaviour without defending it.

## Out of scope, reported rather than fixed

The class doc comment at `src/collection/Filter.mjs:18` lists fifteen operators and the array at `:23` ships sixteen. `doesNotStartWith` is absent from the prose and present in both the array and the implementation at `:247`. Confirmed independently of the ticket. Left alone as Out of Scope directs, so the doc fix can carry its own reasoning; this PR asserts the array's real contents, which is what makes the staleness visible. Filed as #19016 for whoever picks it up.

## AI assistance

Claude Code drafted the spec against the ticket's acceptance criteria. I read every operator's implementation first, ran the expectations against a live `Filter` before writing any of them, and rewrote three that measurement contradicted: `included`/`excluded` argument order, the both-`Date` condition applying only when both sides are Dates, and two `isFiltered` cases of mine that filtered on a property the records did not carry, which made them pass for the wrong reason. The mutation table above is from my own runs.

No file under `src/` is changed.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-20T00:10:33Z

## Thank you — and some orientation I should have led with

My review above was rigorous and cold, which is a habit from reviewing other maintainers who already live in this codebase. You are three artifacts into contributing here and deserved the context alongside the verdict, so here it is.

**Thank you.** Not a formality — specifically:

- You wrote a spec that survives mutation testing. Most first test contributions pin *current output*; yours pins *behaviour*, and the Date-coercion arm caught a `&&`→`||` change I made deliberately to try to fool it.
- You filed #19016 instead of quietly fixing it inside #19015, and said why. That boundary is something we ask of each other constantly and do not always manage.
- You then fixed it in #19017 by a route neither of your own proposed options named, and it is the better one.

### Orientation that is not obvious from outside

**The test tiers.** Neo has three, and which one a test belongs in is a real decision:

```bash
npm run test-unit         # pure logic, no DOM, no workers — where your Filter spec lives
npm run test-components   # a real browser, one component at a time
npm run test-e2e          # full app journeys across real windows
```

Do not run bare `npx playwright test` — Neo uses several custom configs and the bare command silently selects the wrong set.

**Why `setup()` comes before the imports** — you got this right, and the reason is worth knowing: Neo boots a class system before any class module is evaluated, so the import order *is* load-bearing. Copying the shape from a sibling spec, as you did, is the reliable way to get it right.

**Where the reasoning lives.** `learn/agentos/decisions/` holds the ADRs. Tickets cite them by number and they are the closest thing to "why is it like this" — worth a skim when a ticket's premise seems strange.

**The multi-threaded part.** The thing that makes Neo unusual is that your app code runs in a Web Worker, not on the main thread, with the DOM reached through a VDom worker. Most of the subtle bugs in this repo live at those boundaries. `learn/benefits/` is the readable introduction.

**`good first issue`** on #19016 means what it says — it is yours to claim if you want it, and #19017 suggests you already have. `#19007` (Sorter coverage) is adjacent to what you have been doing, if you are looking for a next one.

### One habit worth keeping

You wrote *"if your change makes it red, something is wrong and the spec is the thing to read first"* in #19016. That sentence tells a future reader how to interpret a failure rather than just what to do, and it is rarer than it should be. Keep doing that.

Questions are welcome on any ticket or in Discussions — asking beats guessing, and nobody here will mind.

🖖 Grace

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-20T00:08:14Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only, one new file, no production source and no architectural concept introduced.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the operator matrix is unpinned and this pins it. Verified at the PR head `003d5098a1`: **8 passed**. The claim I actually went after is the one a characterisation spec usually fails — *does it pin anything, or does it only record what happens today?* Two mutations against `src/collection/Filter.mjs`, each reverted:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| `startsWith` loses case folding (`a?.toLowerCase().startsWith(b?.toLowerCase())` → `a?.startsWith(b)`) | **red**, `Error: startsWith should match` — and the labelled assertion names the operator, exactly as the file's own comment says it should |
| Date coercion widened `&&` → `\|\|`, i.e. the mixed Date-vs-number case the spec says is **excluded** | **red** on `both-Date values are coerced with valueOf before the operator runs` |

The second is the one that mattered: it is the subtlest assertion in the file and it turns out to be load-bearing rather than decorative. The thing I looked for and did not find: a vacuous arm. There isn't one — `isDefined(null) === true`, `included('b', [])`, `like('abc', '')` and the empty-prefix `doesNotStartWith` are all genuine boundaries, not middles of ranges.

Three deliberate choices worth naming so a later reader does not "tidy" them away:

- **Iterating `Filter.operators` for the implementation check**, rather than hand-listing. You called it the assertion worth more than the individual cases and that is correct — it is the only one that catches an operator added without a function.
- **`EXPECTED_OPERATORS` restates the array on purpose.** That is a third copy of a list whose duplication you filed #19016 about, and it is still right here: a test that pins a constant must restate it, or it asserts the array equals itself.
- **`doesNotStartWith` pinned as the inverse of `startsWith`** rather than by absolute expectations. For an operator with no doc comment that is the honest form — it survives a deliberate change to the pair without lying about which one moved.

**Findings:**

- [ ] `test.describe.serial` — these are pure static calls with no shared state or ordering dependency, so `describe` alone would do and would let the tier parallelise. Not blocking, and I would not hold the PR for it.

- **Origin Session ID:** eb5c78bf-b451-4ed0-ae82-2e9c60e8cbff

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge**: One finding, measured, and it is **not your mistake** — you inherited it from the sibling you were told to copy.

**`test.describe.serial` truncates this spec's own diagnosis.** Playwright stops a serial block at the first failure, so the arms after it never run. Same head, same mutation, one variable changed:

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| `test.describe.serial` (as shipped) | **1 failed, 2 did not run, 5 passed** |
| `test.describe` | **1 failed, 7 passed** |

Two arms of signal, lost on every real regression. It matters here more than usual: the value of an operator matrix is that a maintainer reading the failure learns *how far* the damage reaches, and a truncated run tells them one operator broke when three did.

Nothing in this file needs it — every arm is a pure static call or a fresh `Neo.create`. Verified rather than assumed: with `.serial` removed and no mutation, **8 passed, three consecutive runs**, and **41 passed** across the whole `collection/` directory.

**You copied it from `Base.spec.mjs:26`, where it is plausibly load-bearing** (a shared collection mutated across tests). So the defect is the tier's, not yours — 36 unit spec files carry `.serial` and 373 do not, and I have proved it unnecessary in exactly one of them. I am filing that as its own ticket rather than generalising from a single file.

**Not blocking.** If you are still awake, dropping `.serial` on line 31 lands it with this PR; if not, it merges as-is and I will carry it. Either is fine.

**One observation for #19016 rather than here:** your `EXPECTED_OPERATORS` is now a third copy of the list, after the source array at `:23` and the doc comment at `:18`. Yours is deliberate — it is the pin, and pins are supposed to be a second copy. But when #19016 fixes the comment there will be three places to edit for one new operator, and whoever takes it should decide whether the comment should just point at the array instead of restating it.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** Pass, and your body is more conservative than your evidence. "Out of scope, reported rather than fixed" for the doc comment is the correct call and you filed it instead of dropping it.
